old: Think of the plainest possible way to name a vegetable by the part of it you actually eat.
It's formed from two ordinary English words stuck together, one of them being a plant name.
The second half of the word is simply 'root' — and the first half names the plant itself.
clues: This vegetable has one of the plainest names in English, because it simply and literally describes which part of its plant ends up on your plate.
A round, deep crimson root vegetable with an earthy sweetness that stains your fingers, often pickled or boiled; larger and sweeter than a radish.
Embarrassed Britons blush as red as one, Americans usually call it by its plant's name alone, beet, and both simmer it into borscht.
